Around Grade 6, families who missed the early years window find an equally strong pathway. Cambridge Lower Secondary develops questioning, collaboration, and independent work ahead of the senior school transition. For those with clear university ambitions abroad, Grade 9 is the decisive entry point, where IGCSE leads directly into the IB Diploma Programme or A Levels, both accepted by leading universities worldwide. Parel and Lower Parel families, your child's ideal stage is waiting. Schedule your admissions consultation today.

Behind this achievement is JBCN's dedicated counselling team, guiding him through every step of the process, from identifying the right opportunity to building a compelling profile.

This is why JBCN is the best international school in Mumbai. Our focus on personalised mentoring and profile-building drives high university placements year after year, producing students who are ready to compete at the highest level globally.

We don't wait for opportunities to come to our students. We help them go after it.

Is the IB curriculum the right choice for your child? The IB Diploma is widely accepted at universities across India and in more than 150 countries, opening doors locally and globally from a single qualification. What truly sets it apart is how it shapes learners beyond academics, developing strong research abilities, critical thinking, and a genuine sense of social responsibility as part of everyday learning. The programme demands dedication and smart time management, but students who stay the course graduate with the kind of intellectual maturity and skills that universities actively look for. Research consistently shows that IB graduates are far more likely to gain admission to leading universities and achieve top honours upon graduation. At JBCN International School, Parel, the best IB school in Parel, every student is backed by highly experienced faculty, tailored university counselling, and a strong mentorship culture that makes the journey as rewarding as the destination. Reach out today and take the first step towards a future without limits!

We are so happy to share that our learners across the Borivali, Parel, Oshiwara and Chembur campuses have done wonderfully in the Cambridge IGCSE 2025-26 February-March examination series! All four campuses recorded a 100% pass rate, with 184 learners appearing across campuses. A combined 131 students received 488 offers and USD 6 million in scholarships from world-class universities such as Imperial College London, UCL, LSE, UC Berkeley, UCLA, University of Toronto, and University of Melbourne. Known as the best IB School in Parel and consistently ranked among the top IB schools in Mumbai, JBCN provides IB Diploma, Cambridge A Levels, IGCSE, and ICSE programmes. featured_reviews.name: Ahana Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely Disappointing and Unethical Admission Process

We recently relocated from Delhi to Mumbai and inquired about admission at JBCN Parel. Most schools clearly informed us if seats were unavailable at the time of inquiry. However, JBCN’s admission team asked us to purchase an admission kit for ₹5,000 just to apply. Since I have two children, I initially enquired only for my elder one, planning to consider the younger one later. As soon as they found out about my younger child, they insisted that I purchase another ₹5,000 admission kit, claiming it would increase the elder one's chances due to the sibling factor.

They then called us to Mumbai for an interaction. Despite my poor health, I attended the session for my elder child, only to be told that there were no seats and we were placed on a waiting list. Shockingly, they called us back the next day for my younger child’s interaction—only to repeat the same thing: no seats available!

This entire process cost us ₹10,000 for admission kits, flight tickets, and 10 days of hotel expenses—completely wasted on false hopes. They misled us emotionally, mentally, and financially. If there are no seats in a particular branch, the school should not push parents to buy admission kits or schedule interactions.

In contrast, Aditya Birla and Edubridge International School were professional and transparent. They informed us upfront that they didn’t have seats. Edubridge even followed up with us when a seat became available and scheduled a school tour accordingly. This is called professionalism.

To make matters worse, JBCN had the audacity to suggest admission at their Chembur branch, expecting a young child to travel from Lower Parel to Chembur daily—without even providing a bus service!

JBCN, please do better. Admissions should be about a child's education, not just a business model to make money. Stop misleading parents and wasting their time and resources.
